summary: Intermittent SSE tail silence after reconnect when auth-cookie jitter occurs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ClipboardAI) reports intermittent missing last paragraph / final tokens when resuming SSE streaming after an auth cookie rotation in their corp-proxy environment. This only appears for long-lived chat sessions that experience an auth cookie refresh mid-stream.

Impact:
- Customer sees 10-20% of resume attempts drop the trailing paragraph on long responses (user-visible lost content).
- Affects production traffic for dedicated customers in us-east-1 using corp-proxy path to Redwood API.
- Customer flagged potential revenue impact for chat users.

Environment:
- Customer: ClipboardAI (dedicated tenancy)
- Client: web single-page app, SSE stream to /v1/generate with Authorization cookie; corp-proxy (internal) performs auth cookie refresh and injects Set-Cookie on backend revalidation.
- Redwood: prod cluster in us-east-1, API fronted by edge-proxy -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start a long-running generation (approx 800-1200 tokens) over SSE.
2) Trigger a cookie refresh at corp-proxy (this happens automatically around cookie expiry; customer forced reauth in test).
3) SSE connection briefly reconnects/resumes with new cookie.
4) Client receives resume fragments but final paragraph (last 1-2 sentences) is missing or silent.

Observed behavior:
- Resume handshake completes, keepalive heartbeats continue, but final 'done' / terminal choice event is not delivered to client in 12% of resumed sessions during tests. Logs show successful upstream forwarding but downstream SSE tail is not flushed to client.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should continue and deliver terminal tokens/metadata. No loss of concluding sentences on reconnect.

Initial logs attached by customer:
- client-logs-clipperai-2026-03-12.txt (attached) includes SSE stream offsets and a short runtime stack trace from their client indicating no JSON parse error.
- network trace shows an auth Set-Cookie on 302 from corp-proxy and immediate follow-up reconnect from client within 200-800ms.

Notes on differences from prior tickets:
- Unlike prior "auth rotation mangled prefix" reports, this case shows the prefix and midstream fragments intact; only trailing tokens are missing. Behavior correlates with timing jitter between token caching and KV priming in serving runtime.
comments: Support (2026-03-13 09:16 UTC) - Jordan Patel: Customer reported 12% failure rate in their internal test during cookie refresh. Provided request IDs 2026-03-13: req-us-east-1-9f2a and req-us-east-1-9f2b. Asked for SRE triage.

SRE (2026-03-13 11:02 UTC) - Riley Chen: Reproduced locally with a scripted proxy that injects Set-Cookie and forces reconnect. Observed resume succeeds but final 'done' event missing when reconnect occurs during serving-runtime KV priming window. Captured worker logs and stack traces.
Customer (2026-03-13 12:40 UTC) - ClipboardAI Eng: Confirmed repro with our staging setup. We can provide a PCAP and scripted replay. This is blocking a release.

SRE (2026-03-14 08:05 UTC) - Riley Chen: Scoped to potential race between auth handoff and KV cache rehydration. Adding edge-proxy and runtime teams to investigate. Temporary mitigation suggested: increase cookie refresh window on corp-proxy to avoid mid-stream refresh.
investigation_notes: 01) Reproducer: small Node script that opens SSE, waits ~2s, then sends a Set-Cookie from proxy and reopens connection. Failure rate mirrors customer (~10-15%).

02) Worker logs (us-east-1 serving-runtime): several resumes show 'kvcache-miss -> priming' around same time as 'session-resume' events. When priming overlaps resume, terminal flush callback sometimes not invoked.

03) Edge-proxy logs: proxy returns 302->Set-Cookie and then closes client socket; client reconnects with new cookie and session-id header. Mapping layer translates session-id to streaming session; mapping seems correct in logs. No 4xx/5xx.
04) Heap/CPU: no OOMs or worker restarts during repro. Latency of priming can vary 50-300ms depending on token length. Failure correlates to priming > 120ms during resume window.

05) Hypothesis: resume handshake race where session state is reattached to a different worker before KV cache priming completes. Flushing terminal metadata depends on a primed callback which may be dropped if worker transition happens. Edge-proxy reattach occurs within 100-800ms which is inside observed priming tail.
06) Related runs: toggling prefetched-kv off removes failure (but increases downstream latency), suggesting priming path involvement.
07) Cross-reference: SUP-20876 contains older auth rotation cases where prefix corruption occurred; link included for context but this is distinct symptom (tail silence).
08) Temporary mitigation recommended: extend cookie refresh grace on corp-proxy to avoid reattach mid-generation; add back-pressure in client to delay reconnect by 500ms on Set-Cookie detection.

09) Action items: (a) add extra instrumentation around priming-flush and resume callback; (b) add a guard to queue terminal flush until priming confirmation or a short debounce; (c) reproduce under load and run canary patch.
resolution: In Progress - mitigation accepted by customer. Implementing guarded terminal-flush in serving-runtime to wait up to 300ms for KV priming confirmation before finalizing stream; if priming not confirmed, fall back to conservative flush with extra metadata. Customer agreed to extend auth refresh window as immediate workaround. Will open PR for patch and run canary in us-east-1.
